standard_prerequisites.name: The bipartite graph Q between the set A and the components D_i of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition, and the maximum matchings M_v leaving a vertex v of D unmatched
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's subsection on the Edmonds-Gallai decomposition (source lines 1054-1072), together with the author's displayed Tutte-Berge and Gallai-Edmonds relations
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects that the strict Hall inequality is proved for, and the family of maximum matchings that the proof inspects.

core_obligations: Maximum matchings leaving v unmatched: for every i and every v in D_i the definition of D gives a maximum matching M_v that leaves v unmatched, and in that matching there is no edge from A to D_i (proof line 1082).
Matching saturating A: the edges of M_v match A to distinct members of the components other than D_i, so Q minus the vertex D_i has a matching saturating A (proof lines 1083-1084).

Hall and strictness: consequently Q has a matching saturating A, so Hall's condition gives |N_Q(S)| >= |S|; if equality held for some non-empty S then deleting any D_i in N_Q(S) would violate Hall's condition, a contradiction, which yields the strict inequality (proof lines 1085-1086).

Consequence for the number of components: in each component of Q the number of components of G_p[D] exceeds the number of vertices of A by at least one, and summing over the components of Q gives the difference m - a = r, so Q has at most r components (proof lines 1088-1089).
proof_roadmap: 对每个 v 取一条不匹配 v 的最大匹配 M_v，它把 A 匹配到除 D_i 之外的分量上，于是 Q 去掉 D_i 后有饱和 A 的匹配。
由 Hall 条件得 |N_Q(S)| >= |S|；若取等号，删掉 N_Q(S) 中任一 D_i 就违反 Hall，矛盾，故为严格不等式。
在每个 Q 的连通分量里 G_p[D] 的分量数比 A 的顶点数至少多一，对全部 Q 求和得差为 r，于是 Q 至多 r 个连通分量。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph of the Edmonds-Gallai decomposition (author lemma at source lines 1073-1079, label lem:strict-hall). The proof (source lines 1081-1090) is a self-contained matching argument: it extracts, for every vertex v of a component D of the D-part, a maximum matching that leaves v unmatched and therefore has no edge from A into that particular component (proof line 1082), uses the remaining edges to match A into the other components and so obtains a matching saturating A in the graph with one component deleted (proof lines 1083-1085), and then upgrades Hall's inequality to a strict one by noting that equality would break Hall after deleting any neighbour (proof line 1086). The closing count converts the strict inequality into the bound on the number of components of the auxiliary graph (proof lines 1088-1089). The argument is short but every step is used. H2.
